Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's performance profile. Our legal/privacy group is starting DPA onboarding and asked us to provide a couple of artifacts so they can sign off quickly: 

1) An annotated dataflow diagram that shows where PII is ingested, transiently stored, and what (if any) telemetry/usage logs leave our tenant.
2) A mapping of PII fields you classify as "sensitive" vs "non-sensitive" for typical LLM ingestion (examples: name, email, payment token - we want columns).
3) A list of subprocessors used in the Hosted offering (region and purpose) and where KMS keys are held.

I'm attaching our onboarding template (WellNest_DPA_Onboarding_Template.pdf) — the privacy team would like artifacts by end of week if possible. Also flag any cross-border transfers or residency constraints we should be aware of; we're EU customers and will bring this up in legal review.

Cheers,
Dana

Hi Dana — looped in from Security & Compliance. I'll summarize the answers and attach the subprocessor roster CSV. See answers inline below.

On Wed, Sep 29, 2026 at 11:03 AM Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com> wrote:
> We can provide an annotated PNG/SVG showing the ingestion->runtime->KV cache->telemetry/export points. Attached is a first sketch (redwood_dataflow_sketch_v1.png).

Correct — that sketch is a good start. We'll annotate the final with the following labels: ingestion gateway (TLS termination), transient request buffer (ephemeral memory on GPU hosts), KV cache (per-model, per-tenant), metrics exporter (aggregated only), and audit logs (write-only append).

> 1) When you say "telemetry/usage logs leave our tenant", do you want: (a) full request traces (token-level) or (b) aggregated operational telemetry (latency/cost metrics)?

Answer: By default Redwood only exports aggregated telemetry (b). Token-level traces are optionally retained for debugging for a limited window (configurable; default 7 days) and are encrypted at rest. Token-level traces require explicit customer opt-in and are subject to access controls. We will note that in the dataflow.

> 2) Residency: you mentioned EU — is EU-only deployment required or is on-demand cross-border for backups acceptable?

Answer: For production EU-only workloads we support a Private EU deployment or Hosted with EU-only tenancy. Backups to non-EU regions are not performed by default for EU-only tenants. Where backups are required to cross borders (rare), they must be encrypted with customer-managed keys; we log and surface any such movement in audit trails.

Subprocessor roster (attached): includes cloud infra providers for hosted control plane, monitoring/CDN, and artifact storage. Each row contains: name, purpose, region(s), processing role, DPA status. Notable items: we use AWS eu-west-1 and GCP europe-west3 for EU-hosted clusters; KMS is customer-managed or Redwood-managed per contract — we mark custody in the roster.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20260928.csv

Next steps:
- We'll produce the finalized annotated dataflow (PNG + SVG) with callouts for PII fields and the three categories you requested.
- We'll export the canonical PII-field mapping CSV for your ingestion examples.
- If WellNest needs the KMS proof-of-control (attestation), we'll prepare a short attestation template for legal to sign — please indicate whether you require HSM-backed keys.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min call with product/compliance this week to walk through the dataflow.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
